title: Otogi 2: Immortal Warriors
subtitle: Raikoh returns with companions
summary: Otogi 2: Immortal Warriors is FromSoftware's Xbox action game, first released in Japan on 25 December 2003. The undead warrior Raikoh returns to confront demons threatening Japan's sacred capital, this time accompanied by allies. The setting draws on Japanese legend, giving the campaign a supernatural character distinct from the machinery and military worlds common elsewhere on the console. Battles are built around movement and force, with the player cutting through demonic opponents in spaces that can be damaged by the struggle. The sequel expands the original game's cast rather than abandoning its atmosphere.
body: Otogi 2: Immortal Warriors is FromSoftware's Xbox action game, first released in Japan on 25 December 2003. The undead warrior Raikoh returns to confront demons threatening Japan's sacred capital, this time accompanied by allies. The setting draws on Japanese legend, giving the campaign a supernatural character distinct from the machinery and military worlds common elsewhere on the console. Battles are built around movement and force, with the player cutting through demonic opponents in spaces that can be damaged by the struggle. The sequel expands the original game's cast rather than abandoning its atmosphere.

Raikoh's companions allow the campaign to be approached through more than one character. Their different capabilities change the feel of moving into an encounter and dealing with its enemies. The player must judge distance and timing while keeping the fight in motion, using attacks to break through opposition rather than waiting in one safe position. The destructible surroundings make that movement visible: a battle leaves its marks on the place where it occurred. Character choice and the physical response of the scenery help distinguish one encounter from another.

Yuki Ichiki composed the music, supporting the game's mixture of myth, violence and otherworldly scenery. Sega published the North American edition in October 2004 and the European release in February 2005. Reviews were generally favourable, but the game reached a relatively small audience. Its later backward-compatible release on newer Xbox systems gave another route to a work that had remained closely associated with the original console. Together with Otogi: Myth of Demons, it shows an earlier side of FromSoftware's action design, before the studio's later international breakthroughs.
